scanner_doubts: ifp_egm.md, lines 260, 261, 267 - all 3 `qe-math-002` hits are false positives: every one is `u'`, the derivative of the utility function, inside `(u' \circ \sigma)`. Line 268 of the lecture says so out loud: 'primes indicate next period states (as well as derivatives)'. Note the pattern - the same `u'(c_t)` at 142, 187, 197, 201 and 218 was correctly skipped, so the guard is working in general; what leaks is `u'` followed by `\circ` or by an opening parenthesis, which §9's 'superscript followed by a factor rather than a relation' test reads as multiplication. Adding `\circ` to the relation side, and treating a single lowercase italic base as non-matrix-like even when followed by a factor, would clear these three.

ifp_egm.md, line 761 vs line 209 - the single `qe-ref-001` hit looks like the wrong one of the two candidates. Line 761 is `* For details see {cite}`ma2020income`` - a bullet-list citation, which the rule text explicitly permits ('Use `{cite}` for standard citations at end of sentences or in lists'). Meanwhile line 209 reads 'As shown in {cite}`ma2020income`,' which is the rule's canonical in-flow case and should be `{cite:t}`; it was not flagged. Line 46 ('The primary source ... is {cite}`ma2020income`') is arguably a third. So the check appears to be keying on 'see {cite}' rather than on author-in-sentence-position, and is both over- and under-firing here.

ifp_egm.md, line 180 - a missing check rather than a wrong count. `{eq}`eqvfs`` names a label that does not exist in this file (the label at 170 is `eqvfs_egm`; `eqvfs` lives in ifp_discrete.md). Per spec §5 a broken `{eq}` ref is Critical severity, but nothing fired: `qe-math-013` catches malformed `{eq}` syntax, as it did in cross_product_trick.md, and this reference is syntactically perfect - it just points nowhere. Since the scanner already collects every `:label:` in the corpus, a same-file label-resolution check would be cheap and would catch the class of copy-paste error that produced this one.
